name: Albinykus
sum: Tiny alvarezsaurid from the Javkhlant Formation of Mongolia, preserved in a crouching, bird-like resting posture.
wsnote: Estimated at under 1 kg; no length estimate in the sources used.
holotype: IGM 100/3004, pelvis and hind limbs in a sitting position, Javkhlant Formation, eastern Gobi, Mongolia.
biology: The first alvarezsaur found crouching with the feet tucked under the body, a posture known from oviraptorids and troodontids.
author: Nesbitt et al. 2011

sources.text: S. J. Nesbitt, J. A. Clarke, and A. H. Turner, M. A. Norell. 2011. A small alvarezsaurid from the Eastern Gobi Desert offers insight into evolutionary patterns in the Alvarezsauroidea. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 31(1):144-153
